video_title: A BIG Advantage For The Lakers & Knicks? Fascinating Financial Updates

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The Lakers are seeking investors for a 73% ownership stake
quotes.excerpt: They are going to be buying at least 73% of the Lakers.
quotes.quote: I was very interested in a story that the Wall Street Journal put out on Friday. They got their hands on the packet that Josh Kushner and Bob Iger are giving to investors about the Lakers' finances. They are going to be buying at least 73% of the Lakers. We will see what happens with the Buss's share and the other shares. Patrick Soon-Shiong, one of the bigger shareholders, has said he is not going to sell. They need to raise somewhere in the neighborhood of $9 billion.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' financial projections suggest a $30 billion valuation in a decade
quotes.excerpt: In this packet, it gives a projection that they think that the Lakers can be worth 30 billion.
quotes.quote: The headline of this story is that in this packet, it gives a projection that they think that the Lakers can be worth 30 billion in a decade. And they have suggested that if things go amazingly, they could be worth as much as 62 billion in a decade. Look, they are trying to get their money.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers expect $144 million from the new national media rights deal
quotes.excerpt: They are expecting to get 144 million from the national rights deal.
quotes.quote: They are expecting to get 144 million from the national rights deal. So Amazon, ESPN, NBC. And there is a little bit more for like overseas rights and radio rights. Every team gets 144. So think of that as, and then the other league revenue, which is other stuff that the teams all get the same share of, sponsorships, licensing, etc., is 32 million. So what they are saying is that the check that is coming from the league that every team gets is roughly 176 million dollars.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Spectrum SportsNet revenue differentiates the Lakers from other NBA teams
quotes.excerpt: This is the deal that differentiates the Lakers from everybody else.
quotes.quote: This is the deal that differentiates the Lakers from everybody else. In the next year, they are expecting to get 180 million. And honestly, there are teams that are getting squat now because the way these regional sports networks have blown up. There are teams that are having to do this on their own. The Mavericks went that route, the Suns have gone that route, the Jazz, there are others. That is an extraordinary number, especially now when there are teams that are getting nothing.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers generate $245 million in ticket and game-day revenue
quotes.excerpt: They make 245 million dollars on tickets and game day operations.
quotes.quote: They make 245 million dollars on tickets and game day operations. That is tickets, parking, concessions, suites, premium.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' local TV revenue remains strong despite financial pressures
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks' financials are also made public because they are a public company.
quotes.quote: The Knicks' financials are also made public because they are a public company. A couple of years ago, MSG Network, which is part of the same parent company as the Knicks, they put their games on, the Knicks were second in local TV revenue. And last year, they were supposed to get 148 million. So the Lakers were up at about 180 and the Knicks were about 150. So a hell of a lot, not in the Lakers' round, but a lot, and that was huge for the Knicks.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks took a $41 million reduction in their local TV deal
quotes.excerpt: They took a 41 million dollar reduction to deal with issues.
quotes.quote: They took a 41 million dollar reduction to deal with issues. Overall, they agreed to reduce the amount of money from their TV deal. The Knicks' contract runs through 29, the Lakers through 32. From 25 through 29, they agreed to take 202 million dollars less. A 28% haircut as MSG Network restructured its deal. And a lot of these local markets, the regional sports network went out of business.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Charter Communications indemnifies MSG Network, protecting Lakers' revenue
quotes.excerpt: The deal that they have made is that they will indemnify Spectrum SportsNet.
quotes.quote: The deal that they have made is that they will indemnify Spectrum SportsNet. So unless Spectrum SportsNet's parent company, which is Charter Communications, goes out of business, as long as that is in business, the Lakers will still get paid.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers generated $680 million in revenue last season
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers last year, even though they had a short playoff run, made 680 million dollars.
quotes.quote: The Lakers last year, even though they had a short playoff run, made 680 million dollars.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.quote: Their playoff revenue was 67 million. I don't even, that feels low to me.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' profit was $129 million, according to Wall Street Journal
quotes.excerpt: The Wall Street Journal said that the Lakers' profit was 129 million.
quotes.quote: The Wall Street Journal said that the Lakers' profit was 129 million. Now you know why Jim Dolan doesn't want to go in the second apron, his profit is only 30 million. They went to the finals.
